answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can bind each identity to a long-lived, non-transferable stake that accrues only through verified work. Each agent must stake onyx into a contract that forbids transfer, delegation, or reuse as collateral; the stake is slashed if the agent is caught colluding. A farm cannot share one stake across many aliases because the trellis of work history it builds is unique per identity, and a lotus of shared custody shows up in the audit trail. A haven of clones without distinct work history gains no weight.
